interpretation: Each thing is most such, compared with the others, when the synonymous quality belongs to the others in virtue of it: fire, the cause of heat to the others, is hottest; so what causes the posterior things to be true is most true; the principles of the eternal beings are cause of being to the others, and as each thing stands to being, so to truth. Read per quality: whatever causes a quality in another is more such than it. The quality is the same on both sides (synonymous); the reading gives no step from causing one quality to being more in another, so it bears on simple priority only through the separate open premise STMT-SIMPLY-PRIOR-IS-CAUSE-OF-BEING. Aquinas cites this chapter in the quarta via for the converse (the maximum causes all in its genus), recorded in AQUINAS-ST-I-Q2-A3-MAXIMUM-CAUSES-GENUS-A.
